title: Why Moses called the prophetic animals unclean
source_text: Ὅθεν εἴπερ ἄλλο τι Μωϋσέως τεθαύμακα, καὶ τὸ τοιοῦτον θαύματος ἀποφανοῦμαι ἄξιον εἶναι, ὅτι φύσεις κατανοήσας ζῴων διαφόρους καὶ εἴτ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ θείου μαθὼν τὰ περὶ αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἑκάστῳ ζῴῳ συγγενῶν δαιμόνων εἴτε καὶ αὐτὸς ἀναβαίνων τῇ σοφίᾳ εὑρὼν, ἐν τῇ περὶ ζῴων διατάξει πάντα μὲν ἀκάθαρτα ἔφησεν εἶναι τὰ νομιζόμενα παρ᾿ Αἰγυπτίοις καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἶναι μαντικὰ, ὡς ἐπίπαν δὲ εἶναι καθαρὰ τὰ μὴ τοιαῦτα. καὶ ἐν ἀκαθάρτοις παρὰ Μωϋσεῖ ἐστι λύκος καὶ ἀλώπηξ καὶ δράκων ἀετός (τε) καὶ ἱέραξ καὶ τὰ ὅμοια τούτοις, καὶ ὡς ἐπίπαν οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς προφήταις εὕροις ἂν ταῦτα τὰ ζῷα εἰς παράδειγμα τῶν κακίστων παραλαμβανόμενα, οὐδέ ποτε δὲ εἰς χρηστὸν πρᾶγμα ὀνομαζόμενον λύκον ἢ ἀλώπεκα. ἔοικεν οὖν τις εἶναι ἑκάστῳ δαιμόνων εἴδει κοινωνία πρὸς ἕκαστον εἶδος ζῴων. καὶ ὥσπερ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἄνθρωποι ἀνθρώπων ἰσχυρότεροί τινες εἰσὶν οὐ πάντως διὰ τὸ ἦθος. τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον δαίμονες δαιμόνων εἶεν ἂν ἐν μέσοις δυνατώτεροι· καὶ οἵδε μὲν τοῖσδε τοῖς ζῴοις χρώμενοι εἰς ἀπάτην τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ καλουμένου ἐν τοῖς λόγοις ἡμῶν ἄρχοντος „τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου,“ ἕτεροι δὲ δι᾿ ἄλλου εἴδους προδηλοῦντες. καὶ ὅρα ἐφ᾿ ὅσον εἰσὶν οἱ δαίμονες μιαροὶ. ὡς καὶ γαλᾶς ὑπό τινων παραλαμβάνεσθαι πρὸς τὸ δηλοῦν τὰ μέλλοντα. καὶ σὺ δὲ παρὰ σαυτῷ κρῖνον ὁπότερόν ἐστι βέλτιον παραδέξασθαι, ὅτι ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸς καὶ ὁ τούτου υἱὸς κινοῦσι τοὺς ὄρνιθας καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ζῷα εἰς μαντικὴν. ἢ οἱ κινοῦντες τὰ τοιαδὶ τῶν ζῴων καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπους παρόντων ἀνθρώπων δαίμονές εἰσι φαῦλοι καὶ, ὡς ὠνόμασε τὰ ἱερὰ ἡμῶν γράμματα, „ἀκάθαρτοι.“
pass_a_gloss: Whence, if (εἴπερ) I have marvelled (τεθαύμακα) at anything else of Moses, I will declare (ἀποφανοῦμαι) also such a thing worthy (ἄξιον) of marvel: that having understood (κατανοήσας) the differing natures (φύσεις διαφόρους) of animals, and whether having learned (μαθών) from the divine (τοῦ θείου) the things about them and about the demons akin (συγγενῶν) to each animal, or also himself ascending (ἀναβαίνων) by wisdom (σοφίᾳ) having found (εὑρών), in the ordinance (διατάξει) about animals he said that all are unclean (ἀκάθαρτα) which are thought among the Egyptians and the rest of men to be prophetic (μαντικά), and for the most part (ὡς ἐπίπαν) clean (καθαρά) those not such. And among the unclean with Moses are wolf (λύκος) and fox (ἀλώπηξ) and serpent (δράκων), eagle (ἀετός) and hawk (ἱέραξ) and the like to these; and in general not only in the Law (νόμῳ) but also in the Prophets (προφήταις) you would find these animals taken (παραλαμβανόμενα) as example (παράδειγμα) of the worst things (κακίστων), and never for a good matter (χρηστὸν πρᾶγμα) named a wolf or fox. There seems then to be some fellowship (κοινωνία) for each form (εἴδει) of demons toward each form of animals. And as among men some men are stronger (ἰσχυρότεροι) than men, not necessarily (οὐ πάντως) because of character (ἦθος), in the same way demons would be more powerful (δυνατώτεροι) than demons in middle things (ἐν μέσοις: indifferents); and these using these animals for deception (ἀπάτην) of men according to the will (βούλημα) of the one called in our writings (λόγοις) 'ruler (ἄρχοντος) of this age (αἰῶνος)', and others foretelling (προδηλοῦντες) through another form. And see to what extent the demons are foul (μιαροί), so that even weasels (γαλᾶς) are taken by some for showing (δηλοῦν) things to come. And you judge (κρῖνον) by yourself which is better to accept: that the God over all (ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεός) and His Son (υἱός) move the birds and other animals to divination (μαντικήν), or those moving such animals and not men, men being present, are wicked (φαῦλοι) demons, and, as our sacred writings (ἱερὰ γράμματα) named them, 'unclean' (ἀκάθαρτοι).
pass_b_english: Hence, if I have admired anything else in Moses, I will declare this too worthy of admiration. He understood the different natures of animals, and, whether he learned from God about them and about the demons akin to each animal, or found it out himself as he rose by wisdom, in his ordinance concerning animals he said that all those reckoned prophetic by the Egyptians and the rest of mankind are unclean, and that, in general, those not of this kind are clean (Leviticus 11:1–47; Deuteronomy 14:3–20). Among the unclean in Moses are the wolf, the fox and the serpent, the eagle, the hawk and the like (Leviticus 11:13–19, 27, 42; Deuteronomy 14:12–18). And, in general, not only in the Law but also in the Prophets you would find these animals taken as examples of the very worst things, and you would never find a wolf or a fox named in connection with anything good.

It seems, then, that there is a certain fellowship between each kind of demon and each kind of animal. And just as among men some are stronger than others, not necessarily because of their character, in the same way some demons may be more powerful than others in morally indifferent matters. Some of them use these animals to deceive men, according to the will of the one who in our teaching is called “the ruler of this age” (John 12:31; 1 Corinthians 2:6), while others give their forewarnings through another kind. And see how foul the demons are, so that even weasels are used by some to reveal the future.

And you, judge for yourself which is better to accept: that the God over all and His Son move birds and the other animals to divination; or that those who move such animals, and not men, though men are present, are wicked demons, and, as our sacred writings have named them, “unclean” (Matthew 10:1).

choices.choice: 'not at all because of their character' -> 'not necessarily because of their character' (οὐ πάντως; old wording overstated the negation); Pass A gloss corrected to match
'in things morally indifferent' -> 'in morally indifferent matters' (word order)
'in our Scriptures' -> 'in our teaching' (ἐν τοῖς λόγοις ἡμῶν, kept distinct from τὰ ἱερὰ γράμματα later in the chapter)
'named for any good purpose' -> 'named in connection with anything good' (εἰς χρηστὸν πρᾶγμα)
'when even weasels are taken by some for revealing' -> 'so that even weasels are used by some to reveal' (ὡς result clause)
'Judge for yourself, then' -> 'And you, judge for yourself' (καὶ σὺ δέ; no 'then' in Greek)

Scripture re-checked: Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14 lists (eagle Lev 11:13 / Deut 14:12, hawk Lev 11:16 / Deut 14:15), John 12:31 and 1 Corinthians 2:6 for 'ruler of this age', Matthew 10:1 'unclean spirits'

Moses' food laws: the unclean-animal ordinance is Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14. The eagle (ἀετός) is named in LXX Leviticus 11:13 and Deuteronomy 14:12, the hawk (ἱέραξ) in Leviticus 11:16 and Deuteronomy 14:15; Origen's 'and the like to these' echoes the LXX formula 'and the like to it'. Wolf and fox are not named but fall under Leviticus 11:27 (four-footed animals that walk on their paws), and the serpent under Leviticus 11:42 (all that go on the belly); cited on that basis, so those verse numbers are an interpretive match, not a verbal one. The general remark about wolves and foxes in the Prophets (e.g. Ezekiel 13:4, Ezekiel 22:27, Zephaniah 3:3) quotes no verse, so it is not cited inline. ‘The ruler of this age’ (ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου): the exact singular phrase is not in the New Testament; it blends John 12:31 ('ruler of this world') with 1 Corinthians 2:6, 8 ('rulers of this age'); both cited. ‘Unclean’ for demons is the Gospels' 'unclean spirits' (e.g. Matthew 10:1; Mark 1:23); one representative verse cited. ἀπὸ τοῦ θείου rendered 'from God' (the divine source is God). ἐν μέσοις = in morally indifferent matters (power not tied to virtue); rendered 'in things morally indifferent'. The full stop after ἦθος and after μιαροί in the staged text is OCR noise. The participial clause 'Some of them use… others give their forewarnings' has no finite verb in Greek (εἶεν ἂν understood); turned into finite English verbs without adding sense.
